newsitem.title: USA: Harassment charges topple top Alaska state judge.
newsitem.headline: Harassment charges topple top Alaska state judge.

text.p: Alaska's top judge relinquished his post amid an investigation into sexual harassment charges but will stay on the state's supreme court, officials said on Thursday.
Allen Compton on Wednesday gave up his position as chief justice of the five-member Alaska Supreme Court, said the Alaska Commission on Judicial Conduct.
The commission gave him a "private admonishment," the least severe sanction it could issue.
After investigating two incidents, occuring in 1995 and 1996, the commission now considers the case closed, said Marla Greenstein, executive director of the commission.
Compton was replaced as chief justice by Warren Matthews, who was elected to that post by his fellow justices, court officials said.
"I feel strongly that the Alaska Court System must not be burdened by the consequences of my personal conduct," Compton said in a statement issued Wednesday.
But the attorney for one woman charging Compton with sexual harassment questioned whether it was appropriate for the justice to remain on the state's highest court.

"It's hard to imagine how a justice who has engaged in sexual harassment can properly decide cases before him that involve discrimination or sexual harassment," said Barbara Norris, an attorney representing a former Compton law clerk.
Her client, Isabel Traugott, a Stanford Law School graduate now working in Maine, was considering filing a civil lawsuit against Compton, Norris said.

Norris said Traugott's career was interrupted by Compton's advances, leaving her job because of the harassment and ending up "doing hourly work with a couple of law firms in California, where she lived with her parents, where she retreated while the whole thing unravelled."
